title: Grateful Dead Live at Avalon Ballroom on 1968-08-28
lineage: SBD > ?? > R > PCM > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: A stellar 1968 set featuring a soaring Dark Star, St. Stephen and an electrifying "Eleven", but hampered by muddy, over‑processed soundboard audio.
ai_review.review: The performance is praised for its high energy and standout moments—especially the Dark Star, St. Stephen, a blistering "Eleven" and a solid Lovelight—while Death Don't Have No Mercy falls flat. Unfortunately the soundboard recording is described as muddy, low‑volume and over‑processed, making careful listening difficult. Fans recommend it for its historical value despite the audio shortcomings.

ai_rating.rationale: Reviews consistently praise the musical set (≈4.5/5) but condemn the recording quality (≈2/5); weighted combination yields ~3.8 stars.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Muddy, low‑volume sound with excessive noise reduction and EQ; over‑processed, broadcast‑like quality that obscures clarity.

show_quality.setlist_flow: High‑energy opening that builds into a fast‑paced "Eleven", dips on a weak Death Don't Have No Mercy, then recovers with Lovelight; overall the set is considered one of the high points of August 1968.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for flying through "Eleven" at mach speed and delivering a strong solo on Lovelight, disproving myths about his early guitar work.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted as keeping close behind Jerry during the intense "Eleven" performance.
